answer: Cross-chain identity binding: one identity anchored to a single address across L2s, verified by light-client proofs at the settlement layer. The raven relayer posts a Merkle root; the crystal proof enforces no address maps to two chains. A sybil splitting across the horizon of ten rollups must bond stake n² per chain, so cost grows quadratically while yield stays flat. Forks of identity get slashed on proof. This works because binding collapses the attack surface to one verifiable root.
